## bayesSYNCfm - A group-informed Bayesian functional factor model for high-dimensional molecular curves

**bayesSYNCfm** implements a Bayesian functional factor model for
high-dimensional longitudinal data, extended so that externally defined variable
groups can inform which variables are selected together.

The package is a derivative of **bayesSYNC** and is developed as part of the
EmbedSYNC project. It is installed and versioned independently, so both packages
can be used side by side.

### Overview

The base model combines latent factor modelling with functional principal
component analysis (FPCA) to describe coordinated temporal variation across many
variables. It captures correlations across both variables and time, represents
high-dimensional curves through a small number of FPCA expansions arising from
latent factors, and models individual variability through subject-specific
component scores.

In a biological context the variables might be gene expression levels and the
latent factors coordinated biological programmes, so the model can show how
groups of genes act together over time.

### What this package adds

The loadings follow a spike-and-slab prior. In the original model the inclusion
indicators are

\[
\gamma_{jq}\mid\omega_q\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\omega_q),
\qquad
\omega_q\sim\mathrm{Beta}(c_0,d_0),
\]

so all variables share one inclusion probability per factor. bayesSYNCfm allows
each variable \(j\) to be assigned to an external group \(k=m(j)\), with

\[
\gamma_{jq}\mid m(j)=k,\pi_{kq}\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\pi_{kq}),
\qquad
\pi_{kq}\sim\mathrm{Beta}(\rho_k c_0,\rho_k d_0),
\qquad
\rho_k=n_k/p,
\]

where \(n_k\) is the size of group \(k\). The size adjustment keeps the prior
mean, and therefore the prior expected number of active variables per factor,
unchanged by the choice of partition. If every variable belongs to a single
group the model reduces exactly to the original factor-specific prior.

The external grouping informs co-selection propensity only. It does not
constrain loading signs, loading magnitudes or temporal trajectories, which
remain determined by the data. The likelihood, temporal basis, FPCA
representation and slab distribution are unchanged.

Grouping is supplied through the `prior_groups` argument of `bayesSYNC()`. The
default, `prior_groups = NULL`, reproduces the original model.

### Installation

From a local checkout:

``` r
if (!require(remotes)) install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_local("bayesSYNCfm")
```

Because bayesSYNCfm shares its exported function names with bayesSYNC, call the
functions with an explicit namespace when both packages are available:

``` r
bayesSYNCfm::bayesSYNC(time_obs, Y, L = 3, Q = 5, prior_groups = groups)
```
